descZh: 1897 年英国作曲家爱德华·埃尔加写给友人多拉·彭尼的密信，信上不是音符而是 87 个弯曲怪异的自创符号，被后世称为「多拉贝拉密码」；埃尔加本人热衷密码游戏，却始终未留密钥，百余年来破译尝试无数，至今无人能解。
descEn: In 1897 the English composer Edward Elgar sent his friend Dora Penny a note written not in music but in 87 strange, curling symbols of his own devising — the "Dorabella Cipher." Elgar loved cipher games yet left no key, and after more than a century of attempts it remains unsolved.
textZh: 密信原文共 87 个符号，分三行排列，仅 24 个符号各不相同，形如带尾巴的圆环与弧线，推测可能对应 24 个拉丁字母。埃尔加在信封上只写「多拉贝拉」（意为「美丽的多拉」）作为署名。有人猜是婚外情表白，有人说是音乐主题的变体，也有人主张只是给多拉的戏谑玩笑——但没有任何解读得到公认。
textEn: The note holds 87 glyphs arranged in three lines, yet only 24 distinct shapes — curling rings and arcs with trailing tails — suggesting a one-to-one mapping onto the 24-letter Latin alphabet. On the envelope Elgar wrote only "Dorabella" ("beautiful Dora"). Theories range from a declaration of love to a musical theme in disguise to a mere prank, but no reading has ever won acceptance.

eraZh: 约 1748–1763 年 · 英国斯塔福德郡
descZh: 英国斯塔福德郡舒格伯勒庄园，一座牧神雕像基座上刻着「OUOSVAVV」八个字母与 D.M. 字样，两百多年无人解出其意；因庄园与圣殿骑士、圣杯传说牵连，这块碑文被《达芬奇密码》式传说笼罩，成为英国最著名的石刻之谜。
descEn: On the base of a marble shepherd statue in Staffordshire's Shugborough Hall stand eight letters — OUOSVAVV — plus the initials D.M. Unsolved for over two centuries and tied to Templar and Holy Grail legends, they form England's most famous stone inscription puzzle.
textZh: 碑文主体为八个字母「O U O S V A V V」，下方另刻 D.M. 两个字母。曾被解读为拉丁文短语「Oro Ut Omnes Sequantur Viam Ad Veram Vitam」（我祈求众人追随通往真正生命之路）的缩略，但这只是众多猜测之一；连查尔斯·狄更斯、达尔文等名人都曾驻足思索，真相至今悬而未决。
textEn: The main line reads O U O S V A V V, with D.M. carved beneath. One popular reading expands it to the Latin "Oro Ut Omnes Sequantur Viam Ad Veram Vitam" ("I pray that all may follow the way to true life") — but it is only one of many guesses. Charles Dickens and Charles Darwin are said to have pondered it; the truth remains unknown.

eraZh: 1968–1974 年 · 美国加州旧金山湾区
descZh: 1960-70 年代活跃于美国加州的连环杀手，自称「黄道十二宫」，向报社寄出多封加密信件自夸罪行；其中 408 密文被高中生夫妇破译，而更复杂的 340 密文直到 2020 年才由民间团队解开，其身份至今成谜。
descEn: A serial killer who terrorized the San Francisco Bay Area in the late 1960s and early 1970s, taunting newspapers with encrypted letters under the self-chosen name "Zodiac." The 408-character cipher was solved by a high-school couple; the harder 340 cipher fell only in 2020, to amateur codebreakers. His identity is still unknown.
textZh: 1969 年 8 月 1 日，杀手把 408 密文一分为三寄给三家报社，要求头版刊载；密文破解后读出一段狂言：「我喜欢杀人，因为杀人实在太有趣了。」同年 11 月他又寄出 340 密文，署名处画着十字准星符号。此后还有一段 13 字符密码至今未破，被称为「我的名字是……」谜题。
textEn: On August 1, 1969, the killer split his 408-character cipher into three parts and mailed them to three newspapers, demanding front-page publication; it decoded to a boast: "I like killing people because it is so much fun." In November he mailed the 340 cipher signed with a crosshair symbol. A final 13-character message — the "My name is..." puzzle — also remains unsolved.

eraZh: 1948 年 · 澳大利亚阿德莱德
descZh: 1948 年澳大利亚萨默顿海滩发现一具无名男尸，衣袋里藏着撕自《鲁拜集》的纸条，上书波斯语「Tamam Shud」（已结束），书中夹页更留有密码；半个多世纪过去，死者身份、死因与密码含义至今成谜，为澳洲最著名的悬案。
descEn: In 1948 a well-dressed man was found dead on Somerton Beach, Adelaide; in his pocket was a scrap torn from a Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam reading "Tamam Shud" (Persian for "it is ended"), and a copy of the book found later bore a cipher. More than seventy years on, his identity, cause of death and the cipher's meaning remain unknown — Australia's most celebrated cold case.
textZh: 男尸口袋中的纸条写着「Tamam Shud」——波斯语「已结束」。警方循线找到原书，书末印着电话号码，书后空白页上留下一行五组字母的密码，下方另有五行字母串；密码学家尝试多种解法均告失败，甚至有人猜测与冷战间谍有关。至今这行密码仍静静躺在档案中。
textEn: The scrap in the dead man's pocket read "Tamam Shud" — Persian for "it is ended." Tracing it led police to the original book, which contained a phone number and, on its blank endpapers, a cipher: five letter groups with five more lines below. Cryptologists have tried every approach without success, and theories drift toward Cold War espionage. The cipher still sits unsolved in the case file.

eraZh: 约公元前 1700 年 · 克里特岛费斯托斯
descZh: 1908 年在克里特岛费斯托斯王宫出土的黏土圆盘，两面以螺旋排列 45 种印刷式符号，约属公元前 1700 年，为世界上最早「活字印刷」的实物证据之一；其语言、用途与内容至今没有公认解读，是考古学与密码学交织的著名未解之谜。
descEn: Unearthed in 1908 at the Minoan palace of Phaistos, Crete, this fired-clay disc bears 45 distinct stamped symbols arranged in spirals on both faces — possibly the world's earliest "movable type" — dated to around 1700 BC. No agreed reading of its language, purpose or message has ever been reached.
textZh: 圆盘直径约 16 厘米，双面各有螺旋状符号环带，共刻 241 个印记，由 45 种不同符号组成，如人形、鱼、鸟、船与植物；符号以模具逐枚压印而成，暗示存在成批「印刷」的文字传统。有学者主张其为祈祷文或占卜用具，也有人怀疑是赝品，迄今尚无定论。
textEn: The disc is about 16 cm across, its two faces covered in spiral bands bearing 241 impressions made from 45 distinct sign-types — running men, fish, birds, ships and plants. Each sign was pressed with a separate stamp, hinting at a tradition of mass "printing." Scholars have proposed prayers, board-game pieces or even a forgery; no verdict has been reached.

eraZh: 约公元前 1800–1450 年 · 克里特岛与爱琴海
descZh: 米诺斯文明使用的书写系统，刻于泥板、印章与祭器上，约 1400 件遗存；其后续文字线形文字 B 已于 1952 年被破译，证明是希腊语，而线形文字 A 所记录的语言至今无法确定，被称为爱琴海考古最大的未解之谜之一。
descEn: The script of Minoan civilization, preserved on clay tablets, seals and votive objects in some 1,400 inscriptions. Its successor, Linear B, was deciphered in 1952 and proved to be Greek; Linear A's underlying language remains unidentified — one of the great open questions of Aegean archaeology.
textZh: 线形文字 A 符号多为线条化的象形，兼有表音与计数记号，出现于宫殿泥板与宗教祭器上，常与「祭献清单」关联；学者试以希腊语、吕基亚语乃至印欧语系以外的语言破译，皆未获共识。1952 年迈克尔·文特里斯破译线形文字 B 时，曾寄望借此反推 A，最终仍功亏一篑。
textEn: Linear A consists of simplified pictographs with syllabic and numeral signs, found on palace tablets and cult vessels, often reading like offering inventories. Attempts to match it to Greek, Luwian or any known family have won no consensus; even Michael Ventris, after deciphering Linear B in 1952, hoped to work backward to A — in vain.

eraZh: 约 18–19 世纪 · 复活节岛（拉帕努伊）
descZh: 复活节岛上的刻字木板，以「诵唱」之意得名，岛民称其为会说话的木头；现存约 25 件残片，符号呈人鸟兽等象形与几何形，可能是波利尼西亚唯一的本土文字，1860 年代岛民识读传统中断后至今无人能解。
descEn: Rongorongo — "the chants" — are inscribed wooden tablets from Easter Island, which the islanders called "talking wood." About 25 fragments survive, their glyphs pictographic and geometric forms of humans, birds and other motifs. Possibly the only indigenous script of Polynesia, it lost its last readers in the 1860s and remains undeciphered.
textZh: 木板上刻着成排的符号，最特别之处在于阅读方向：每行从下往上读，隔行倒转 180 度，形成「牛耕式」蜿蜒的阅读路径；符号有约 400 个变体。传说木板记载着创世歌谣与族谱，1864 年传教士的记载提到岛民尚能「唱」读，此后文字失传，解读终成绝响。
textEn: The tablets bear rows of glyphs read bottom-to-top, with every other line rotated 180° in a "boustrophedon" serpentine path; roughly 400 glyph variants are known. Legend says they record creation chants and genealogies, and a missionary in 1864 noted islanders could still "sing" them — then the tradition died and the script fell silent forever.

eraZh: 1918 年发明 · 美国波士顿
descZh: 美国发明家约翰·F·伯恩 1918 年发明的便携密码机，他宣称该密码「不可破译」，1920 年代向军方与国务院推销却被拒；2010 年伯恩家族解密算法后，其原理公开——至今未发现可行的普通破解法，被视为天才的密码孤本。
descEn: A portable cipher machine invented in 1918 by American John F. Byrne — James Joyce's close friend — who insisted it was unbreakable. Rejected by the military and State Department in the 1920s, its algorithm stayed secret until Byrne's family released it in 2010; no practical shortcut attack is known even now.
textZh: 混沌密码的独特之处在于「双混字母表」：每次加密后，两个字母表都会按固定规则自行重组，使同一明文字母在不同位置加密成不同密文，旧式频率分析因此失效。伯恩曾将用其加密的挑战文本寄给《科学美国人》悬赏破解，无人成功；2010 年公开算法时，爱好者依说明在纸上即可复现整机。
textEn: The machine's genius lies in two permuting alphabets: after every encipherment both alphabets re-arrange themselves by fixed rules, so the same plaintext letter becomes different ciphertext at different positions — defeating old frequency analysis. Byrne offered the cipher to Scientific American as a challenge and nobody broke it; when the algorithm went public in 2010, hobbyists rebuilt the whole machine on paper from the description.

eraZh: 1969 年 11 月 · 美国旧金山
descZh: 1969 年 11 月 8 日黄道杀手寄给《旧金山纪事报》的 340 字符密文，51 年间令 FBI 与全球爱好者束手无策；2020 年 12 月，三人民间团队以交叉比对法破译，读出「我希望你们在抓捕我时玩得开心」等语句，成为近年最轰动的民间密码破解。
descEn: The 340-character cipher mailed to the San Francisco Chronicle on November 8, 1969, defied the FBI and hobbyists alike for 51 years. In December 2020 a three-person amateur team cracked it by cross-matching repeated patterns, reading "I hope you are having lots of fun in trying to catch me" — the decade's most sensational civilian codebreak.
textZh: 破解文本全文大意：「我希望你们在抓捕我时玩得开心。我不怕毒气室，因为它会把我更快送上天，因为我现在已经有足够多的奴隶为我劳作……」，句中提及「天堂」与「奴隶」，呼应杀手自比极乐主宰的幻想；其余段落仍含拼写错误与自创词，学界对破解结论仍有保留意见。
textEn: The plaintext runs roughly: "I hope you are having lots of fun in trying to catch me. I am not afraid of the gas chamber because it will send me to paradice all the sooner because I now have enough slaves to work for me..." — complete with misspellings like "paradice" and fantasies of slaves and paradise. Some researchers still dispute the solution.
